items.text: Tennessee halted scheduled executions after Christa Pike appeared still breathing following a lethal injection attempt.
items.detail: Witnesses said Pike still appeared to be breathing about an hour after pentobarbital was administered late Wednesday at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville; she was taken to a hospital. Gov. Bill Lee ordered a third-party review and said the remaining scheduled execution will not be carried out this year. Earlier Wednesday the Supreme Court vacated a Sixth Circuit stay (Nelsen v. Pike, 26A428), clearing Tennessee to proceed before the warrant expired at midnight; Justices Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson dissented. Pike, 50, was convicted of the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer and was the only woman on Tennessee's death row.
items.why: A failed lethal injection and a statewide pause on further executions, after the Supreme Court cleared the state to proceed the same day.

items.text: A State Department rule removed Syria from the blanket ban on U.S. defense-trade licenses.
items.detail: The International Traffic in Arms Regulations final rule, effective Oct. 1, takes Syria off ITAR §126.1's list of countries subject to a policy of denial for defense exports and imports. License requests will be reviewed case by case. The change follows the secretary's Aug. 19 defense-trade policy shift after statutory barriers, including terrorism-related restrictions, were lifted or waived. Belarus, Burma, China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Venezuela remain on the denial list.
items.why: Opens a path to licensed U.S. defense sales and services to Syria that were previously denied by default.

items.text: USDA rewrote Rural Energy for America grants so projects must already be built before applicants can apply.
items.detail: The Rural Business-Cooperative Service final rule, published Oct. 1 and effective Oct. 16, shifts REAP renewable-energy and efficiency grants to a post-completion model using 12 months of actual performance data. It bars solar and wind systems on Farm Service Agency–certified cropland, bars components from foreign-adversary countries, limits applicants to highest-level owners, and replaces state contests with national scoring. Comments are due Nov. 2.
items.why: Changes who can get rural energy grants and when, with new farmland and foreign-component limits.

items.text: The Yankees, Padres and White Sox each swept their MLB Wild Card Series; the Phillies forced a Game 3.
items.detail: On Wednesday the Yankees beat the Red Sox 9-2, the White Sox beat the Astros 7-3 and the Padres beat the Cubs 4-1 to advance to the Division Series. The Phillies beat the Braves 4-3 in 10 innings, forcing a decisive Game 3 on Thursday.
items.why: Three Wild Card Series are over; one winner-take-all game remains before the Division Series.

items.text: The Senate confirmed Keith Sonderling as Labor secretary.
items.detail: The nomination was confirmed 47-41 on a party-line vote late Wednesday (roll call 256), with 12 senators not voting. Sonderling had been serving as acting labor secretary. The vote came after the Senate earlier Wednesday invoked cloture on the nomination 53-47.
items.why: Fills the Cabinet labor post that oversees workplace rules, wages and federal labor enforcement.

items.text: The United States ended its anti-ISIS military mission in Iraq, withdrawing the last U.S. troops after more than two decades.
items.detail: Operation Inherent Resolve's Iraq mission concluded Wednesday under a 2024 Baghdad-Washington transition plan; roughly 2,500 remaining U.S. forces left, with Iraq assuming full responsibility for security against ISIS remnants. Iran and aligned groups cast the exit as a win. The U.S. and Iraq say they will shift to a bilateral security relationship; concerns remain about militia influence and residual ISIS threats without U.S. air and intelligence support on the ground.
items.why: Closes a major U.S. combat footprint in Iraq and reshapes regional security against ISIS and Iran-aligned forces.

items.text: A Flydubai pilot stabbed the other pilot on a Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight and apparently tried to crash the plane, Israel's prime minister said.
items.detail: Flight FZ1073 (Dubai to Tel Aviv) transmitted emergency codes including 7500 (unlawful interference), descended thousands of feet, and diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia; Israel scrambled warplanes amid hijacking fears. Netanyahu said one pilot stabbed the other and apparently tried to crash the Boeing 737; Flydubai confirmed a flight-deck altercation, said all passengers were safe, and said motives remain under investigation. Saudi airport officials said both pilots were hospitalized; Saudi and UAE authorities opened investigations.
items.why: An in-flight attack on an Israel-bound jet that briefly looked like a hijacking and nearly became a mass-casualty crash.

items.text: Iran received a formal U.S. response to its proposal to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
items.detail: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented the U.S. response to President Masoud Pezeshkian at Wednesday's cabinet meeting after receiving feedback via Qatari mediators in Doha on Tuesday night, officials said. The contents were not disclosed. A Reuters-briefed official said the main disagreement is the sequencing of a seven-day trust-building plan, not its components. President Trump had publicly rejected Iran's earlier offer days ago; mediators kept working. Pezeshkian said Iran would seek a "win-win" agreement.
items.why: Moves ceasefire and Hormuz reopening talks after Trump's public rejection; the strait carries about a fifth of the world's oil.

items.text: The Ratepayer Protection Act and the Stop Insider Trading Act, both House-passed bills, failed in the Senate.
items.detail: Both needed 60 votes to advance and fell short the same afternoon. The Ratepayer Protection Act (vote 254, 57-43) would have pushed state utility regulators to keep large data-center power and water costs off residential ratepayers; four Democrats — Hassan, Klobuchar, Ossoff and Warnock — joined Republicans; the House had passed it 417-3. The Stop Insider Trading Act (vote 253, 53-47, party-line) would have barred members, spouses and dependent children from buying new publicly traded stocks while allowing sales with advance notice and letting them keep existing holdings. Separately, the Senate voted 53-47 to invoke cloture on Keith Sonderling’s nomination as Labor secretary (vote 255), clearing a procedural step toward a final confirmation vote.
items.why: Blocks near-term Senate action on data-center ratepayer costs and on congressional stock-trading limits before the midterm recess.

items.text: Russian strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight killed four people, including a child, and hit power infrastructure.
items.detail: President Zelenskyy said the main targets were energy infrastructure in Kyiv and the surrounding region. The Russian Defense Ministry claimed hits on a hydroelectric plant, a thermal plant, a substation, an energy storage facility and a data center; Ukrainian officials did not confirm those specific targets and reported hits on civilian areas in at least four Kyiv districts. Ukraine's air force said Russia is using ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones that are hard to intercept.
items.why: Continues Russia's campaign against Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter; not a change in the war's scope.

also.text: The Yankees, Braves, Padres and White Sox each won Game 1 of their MLB Wild Card Series on Tuesday.
also.detail: Yankees beat the Red Sox 9-0; Braves beat the Phillies 5-3; Padres beat the Cubs 8-0; White Sox beat the Astros 6-3. All four series are best-of-three; Game 2s are Wednesday. Teams that take a 1-0 lead have historically won the Wild Card Series about 88% of the time.
also.why: Sets the early postseason bracket; series continue Wednesday.

also.text: Armada Acquisition Corp. II shareholders approved the Evernorth XRP-treasury merger, a step toward a planned Nasdaq listing as XRPN.
also.detail: The noon-ET special meeting cleared the business-combination vote, according to meeting attendees reported by crypto.news; an official SEC 8-K with final tallies had not posted by evening research. Proxy materials project at least about 473 million XRP at closing if the deal closes. Approval is not the same as listing or trading — remaining closing conditions and Nasdaq requirements still apply, with completion targeted for late 2026.
also.why: Advances a heavily watched crypto SPAC toward a public XRP treasury vehicle; listing and closing are still ahead.

week.text: The Transportation Department finalized lower fuel economy standards for new cars and light trucks.
week.detail: New vehicles must average 34.9 miles per gallon by model year 2031, down from about 50 mpg under the previous rules. The rule covers model years 2022 through 2031, ends the credit-trading program automakers use to meet the standards starting in 2028, and changes how vehicles are classified as cars or light trucks in 2030. The department estimates it lowers the average new-vehicle price by about $1,300. Environmental groups criticized the change.
week.why: A final, binding national rule for every new car and light truck sold in the U.S.; it can be challenged in court or changed by a later rule.

week.text: A 100% Section 232 tariff on most patented drug imports took effect for companies not covered by the July phase-in.
week.detail: Under Proclamation 11020, the additional duties applied to Annex III companies from July 31 and to all other companies' patented pharmaceuticals and ingredients entered on or after 12:01 a.m. Eastern on Sept. 29. Rates range from 0% to 100% depending on patent status, country, onshoring agreements and use; generics and many U.S.-origin products are excluded. Partner jurisdictions such as the U.K. can face 0%, and EU/Japan/South Korea/Switzerland/Liechtenstein patented articles face 15%.
week.why: A binding nationwide tariff on patented drug imports for most remaining companies; it can raise list prices or shift supply chains.

week.text: President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war.
week.detail: Iran had offered terms to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the route for about a fifth of the world's oil shipments, and end the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, now in its seventh month. Iran's foreign minister said Iran will wait for a formal U.S. response before abandoning ceasefire talks. Eight U.S. Marines were injured by an Iranian missile in the strait on Sept. 14.
week.why: Determines whether an active war involving the U.S. continues and whether a key global oil route reopens.

upcoming.text: Korea Blockchain Week wraps in Seoul (main conference Sept. 30–Oct. 1).
Supreme Court opens its new term and hears Suncor Energy v. Boulder County.
upcoming.detail: Whether federal law bars state-law lawsuits seeking damages from oil and gas companies for climate change.
